claims.claim_text: In 2024, Carabao Group pursued its business in alignment with the Company’s vision towards the goal of “World Class Product, World Class Brand,” while remaining committed to continuous sales growth in both domestic and international markets.
The Company’s sustainability operations follow the framework of sustainable practices under the concept of “Building Society of Opportunities for a Brighter Living.”

The Company has operated cautiously while steadfastly adhering to its announced sustainability goals, contributing as a driving force for Thailand to achieve sustainable development goals by 2030 and Net Zero by 2068.

2024 saw Carabao Energy Drink become the leader in the energy drink industry in Thailand, with total revenue reaching 20.964 billion baht, an increase of 11.19%, and a net profit of 2.843 billion baht, up 47.77% compared to 2023.

The Company has emphasized reducing negative impacts from its operations and creating positive social and environmental effects. This includes installing solar rooftops to reduce reliance on fossil fuels and minimizing packaging weight to decrease the use of aluminum, glass, and paper in the production process.
Last year we achieved a 4.9% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions per product unit, exceeding our target of 4.3%.
The Company established a climate strategy to address risks and opportunities arising from climate change, aiming for a 30% reduction in greenhouse gas emissions.
Within 18 months after the launch, become the first challenger of the local energy drink market.
Exporting the finished goods to 15 countries.
Established DCM As a distributor for the Group.
Established APG as a manufacturer and producer of glass bottles.
Introduced Start Plus, a zinc-contained mineral drink, and rebranded it as Carabao Sport in 2018.
Carabao Group began trading on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in November 2014.
Started establishing own distribution centers in 2015 with a target to cover over 300,000 retail shops in Thailand.
CBG invested in ICUK and carbonated Carabao energy drinks were firstly marketed in the UK in 2016.
Become a principal partner sponsor of Chelsea Football Club in 2016.

Carabao Group is committed to continuously developing and improving its operations to conduct business responsibly towards society and the environment, while also collaboratively fostering a strong and sustainable economy and community for the country—both now and in the long term.
Sustainable development is at the core of the Company’s highest priorities in its business operations.

The Company must establish a sustainability management framework to guide its operations in driving the organization across economic, social, and environmental dimensions, based on good corporate governance principles, under the concept of ‘Building a Society of Opportunities for a Brighter Living.’

This diagram presents the sustainability framework of Carabao Group, structured around three pillars: Better Economy, Better Quality of Life, and Better Environment. Each pillar is associated with specific Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and key focus areas, all contributing to the central mission of 'Building a Society of Opportunities for a Brighter Living.'
Better Economy: SDGs: 3, 8, 9, 12, 17 (icons shown). Focus areas: Sustainable sourcing and supply chain, Innovation and technology, Product and service development

Better Quality of Life: SDGs: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 10 (icons shown). Focus areas: Talent development and retention, Consumer’s health and nutrition, Labor practices, Occupational health and safety, Community and Social Well-being
Better Environment: SDGs: 6, 7, 9, 12, 13, 14, 15 (icons shown). Focus areas: Climate management, Water stewardship, Waste management, Energy management, Packaging and circularity, Biodiversity

Carabao Group believes that corporate governance is a fundamental foundation that promotes transparency, accountability, and sustainability.
The Company has implemented a corporate governance policy consisting of five key areas.
The Company has a clear corporate governance structure and a system for monitoring operations supported by the oversight of the Internal Audit Committee, which consists of independent directors.
There is an internal auditing process to effectively control and oversee audits, with risk assessments conducted at all levels of operations.

The Board of Directors has resolved to establish a Committee for Sustainable Development to summarize good sustainability principles beyond just good corporate governance, and to support the Board in integrating sustainability into the organizational culture.
A Sustainability Team has been established to report to the Committee for Sustainable Development and the Executive Committee, which is responsible for the Company’s sustainability efforts.

The Company’s risk management is overseen by the Board of Directors through the Audit Committee and the Risk Management Committee to monitor risks and the effectiveness of the organization’s risk management efforts.

Compliance with the code is linked to employee compensation and performance evaluations, with disciplinary actions and Company regulations in place for violations, including verbal warnings, written reprimands, and termination, as appropriate.

Carabao Group is a leading energy drink manufacturer in the country, using a significant amount of water in the production process.

The Company utilizes water from external water suppliers to mitigate the risk of water shortages in the production process and enhance its competitiveness by being able to meet the demands of its partners.
Reuse RO Reject water from the CBD factory to produce trap water for use in the APG and ACM factories.
Commenced operations from May to December 2024, reusing 55,736 cubic meters of water.
Control the amount of water used in the production process of 250 ml ACM cans to be less than 0.16 cubic meters per kilogram of cans.
Commenced operations from March to December 2024, achieving a total water consumption reduction of 25,560 cubic meters.
The Company has established a Water Operations Team to implement strategies for sustainable water management.
The company was able to reduce water withdrawal by 7.09% in 2024.
The Company has implemented various measures through its effective water management program.
The company minimizes freshwater withdrawal by adjusting the RO water system flow to reduce the percentage of rejected water in the system.
This initiative results in annual water savings of approximately 758 cubic meters per year.
Reuse RO Reject water from the CBD factory to produce tap water for use in the CBD, APM, APG and ACM factories which can reduce water usage by 55,736 cubic meters per year.
Adjust the RO water system flow to reduce the percentage of reject water in the system which can reduce water usage by 758 cubic meters per year.
The CBD factory reuses hot water for can washing (RO) by processing it and feeding it into a deaerator to remove air or oxygen, which can reduce water usage by 7,656 cubic meters per year.
The CBD factory reuses condensate water from the mixing process and hot water boiling process by feeding it back into the deaerator, which can reduce water usage by 30,341 cubic meters per year.

By lowering steam pressure from 6.5 bar to 5 bar, reusing condensate and hot water, and improving steam efficiency, the factory reduced natural gas consumption by 330.58 MMBTU per year, saving 119,707.40 baht annually.

By optimizing the on/off control of pathway lighting between buildings, the APG Factory reduced electricity consumption by 26,280 kilowatt-hours per year, resulting in an annual savings of 105,120 baht.

Repairing the furnace structure, controlling oxygen ratio, and conducting maintenance activities led to improved furnace condition and reduced heat loss, with a reduction in natural gas consumption by 10,561 MMBTU per year, resulting in annual savings of 3,685,700 baht.

ACM Factory reduced natural gas consumption by 9,806 MMBTU per year, saving 3,566,650 THB baht year, and reduced electricity consumption by 2,377,084 kilowatt-hours per year, saving 8,908,910 baht per year.
The replacement of aluminum cooling tower fan blades with lighter fiber blades resulted in reduced motor load, extended equipment lifespan, and significant annual electricity and cost savings.

224 energy-efficient high bay lights were installed, maintaining brightness while reducing energy consumption, reducing electricity usage by 26,138 kilowatt-hours per year, resulting in an annual cost saving of 97,960 baht.

claims.claim_text: Carabao Group prioritizes biodiversity management to support sustainable business operations.
The Company is committed to integrating biodiversity protection into its operations.
This includes assessing risks related to biodiversity and developing measures to prevent and mitigate potential impacts from its activities.
The Company promotes collaboration with partners and raises awareness about natural resource conservation.
It aims to develop responsible production processes to ensure sustainable business practices that do not negatively impact biodiversity.
The Company is committed to regularly assessing biodiversity risks using tools like the WWF Biodiversity Risk Filter to identify and manage risks in its operational areas.
If the Company develops new factory construction projects, it will avoid encroaching on forests or high-biodiversity areas to maintain ecological balance.
The Company focuses on efficient management of water, energy, and raw materials to reduce natural resource consumption and waste generation.
The Company implements wastewater treatment systems that comply with standards before discharging into public water sources, minimizing environmental impact.
The Company continuously records and monitors greenhouse gas emissions from its operations to improve efficiency and performance.
The Company encourages suppliers to assess biodiversity risks related to their operations, implement mitigation measures, and participate in local biodiversity conservation and restoration.
The Company assessed biodiversity risks at its operational sites using the WWF Risk Filter Suite.
The assessment covered four production facilities—CBD, APG, ACM, and APM—located in Bang Pakong District, Chachoengsao Province, spanning a total area of 28.8 hectares (180 rai).
The results indicated that the four factory sites have a high biodiversity risk level (3.5).
The Company assessed biodiversity risks at its operational sites using the WWF Risk Filter Suite.
The results indicated that the four factory sites have a high biodiversity risk level (3.5).
The Company has expanded its biodiversity risk assessment to cover upstream and downstream activities, aiming to reduce future risks.

Results of biodiversity risk assessment shows that in the upstream activities, most areas are classified as having very high biodiversity risk (4.13–4.44) while in the downstream activities, most areas are classified as having moderate to high biodiversity risk (3.25–3.5).
